Name: C4 Context
Keywords: c4 context; system context; actors; external systems; c4 level 1
Edge Semantics: solid arrow = user/system interaction; label with protocol or intent, no internal detail
Anti-Patterns: showing internal service boundaries or DB schemas at context level; overcrowding with more than 7 nodes
Example Scenario: explain who uses a ride-hailing system and which external systems it talks to

Name: C4 Container
Keywords: c4 container; container diagram; deployable units; c4 level 2; service boundaries
Edge Semantics: labeled arrows show protocol (HTTP/gRPC/AMQP) between deployable containers
Anti-Patterns: mixing class-level detail into container boxes; omitting protocol labels on edges
Example Scenario: break a chat system into deployable containers: web client, API gateway, chat service, message queue, database

Name: C4 Component
Keywords: c4 component; internal modules; class diagram; c4 level 3; implementation detail
Edge Semantics: arrows between internal modules/classes inside one container; rarely needed for system design
Anti-Patterns: using this instead of container level for system-design interviews; exposing implementation classes to non-technical audiences
Example Scenario: show the internal module breakdown inside a single order-service container

Name: Request Lifecycle
Keywords: request lifecycle; request path; hop by hop; latency breakdown; request trace; vẽ luồng yêu cầu; sơ đồ hệ thống yêu cầu
Edge Semantics: sequential solid arrows = one request's hop-by-hop path; annotate each hop with latency
Anti-Patterns: showing parallel/async paths as if sequential; omitting where the response returns
Example Scenario: trace a single API-gateway request from browser to database and back

Name: Sequence Flow
Keywords: sequence diagram; message sequence; actor lanes; protocol exchange; uml sequence
Edge Semantics: time-ordered arrows between actors/lanes; dashed = async callback, solid = sync call
Anti-Patterns: mixing multiple unrelated flows in one lane set; missing top-to-bottom time ordering
Example Scenario: walk through the exact message sequence for a payment authorization call

Name: Data Pipeline
Keywords: data pipeline; etl; streaming pipeline; data flow; transformation stages
Edge Semantics: directional arrows show transformation stages; label with data format or volume
Anti-Patterns: hiding backpressure or failure paths; treating batch and streaming stages identically
Example Scenario: show how raw clickstream events get transformed into a ranked news feed index

Name: Event-Driven Pub/Sub
Keywords: pubsub; event driven; fanout; kafka topic; event bus
Edge Semantics: publish arrows into topic hub, subscribe arrows fanning out; dashed = at-least-once delivery
Anti-Patterns: drawing point-to-point lines instead of hub fan-out; forgetting the DLQ path for poison messages; drawing one lone subscriber -- a single consumer is not a fan-out; the Node Kinds list carries a worker plus a webhook-dispatcher plus a metrics-collector on purpose so a truthful fanout also clears hub-spoke's 5-spoke advisory floor (one kind becomes the hub)
Example Scenario: publish an order-placed event and fan it out from the bus to a named topic, a worker pool, a webhook dispatcher, a metrics collector, and a dead-letter queue

Name: Deployment Topology
Keywords: deployment topology; infra layout; multi-az; multi-region; cluster placement; k8s; kubernetes; pods; services; deployment
Edge Semantics: solid = network path between deployment units; dashed = failover/standby path
Anti-Patterns: showing application logic instead of infra placement; ignoring which AZ/region a node lives in
Example Scenario: show how a video-streaming service is deployed across multiple regions and availability zones

Name: Network Topology
Keywords: network topology; network diagram; subnet; service mesh; routing links
Edge Semantics: solid = physical/logical network link; label with protocol and port
Anti-Patterns: conflating network topology with application call graph; omitting subnet/zone boundaries
Example Scenario: show how load balancer, reverse proxy, and service mesh nodes are network-connected for routing

Name: State Machine
Keywords: state machine; fsm; state transitions; circuit breaker states; transaction states
Edge Semantics: labeled arrows = state transition triggers; self-loop = retry within same state
Anti-Patterns: drawing every possible transition (state explosion); omitting the triggering event label on each arrow
Example Scenario: model the closed, open, and half-open states of a circuit breaker protecting a payment provider

Name: Caching Strategy
Keywords: caching strategy; cache hit miss; ttl; cdn cache; read-through cache
Edge Semantics: solid = cache hit path, dashed = cache miss fallthrough to origin
Anti-Patterns: omitting the miss/fallthrough path; not labeling TTL or eviction policy
Example Scenario: show how a CDN and Redis cache sit in front of the database for a news feed read path

Name: Scaling Story
Keywords: scaling story; growth narrative; evolution timeline; scale phases; architecture evolution; ccu; load tiers; growth thresholds
Edge Semantics: arrows connect the same logical component across time phases; annotate with scale metric (users/QPS)
Anti-Patterns: compressing all phases into one static snapshot; missing the metric that triggered each phase
Example Scenario: narrate how a chat platform evolved from a monolith to a sharded microservice architecture at scale

Name: Queue Worker
Keywords: queue worker; task queue; worker pool; job distribution; dlq
Edge Semantics: solid = enqueue/dequeue path; dashed = retry back to queue or to DLQ after max attempts
Anti-Patterns: unbounded worker fan-out with no backpressure shown; missing the DLQ path
Example Scenario: distribute crawl tasks from a queue to a pool of worker processes for a web crawler

Name: Auth Flow
Keywords: auth flow; oauth; sso; login sequence; token exchange
Edge Semantics: time-ordered arrows across actor lanes; dashed = redirect, solid = direct token exchange
Anti-Patterns: hiding the redirect hops; not labeling which token type is exchanged at each step
Example Scenario: walk through the OAuth 2.0 authorization code redirect flow between a browser, an identity provider, and an API

Name: CQRS Saga
Keywords: cqrs; saga pattern; compensating transaction; command query separation; distributed transaction
Edge Semantics: solid = command path (write model), dashed = compensating action on saga failure
Anti-Patterns: merging the read and write models into one store; omitting the compensating transaction path
Example Scenario: coordinate a distributed transaction across services using a saga orchestrator with separate read and write stores

Name: Comparison
Keywords: comparison; vs; versus; side by side; with and without; before after; tradeoff panes
Edge Semantics: per-pane only -- no edge crosses a gutter; solid = the pattern's main path; delta edges take the accent
Anti-Patterns: panes drawn with different visual vocabulary (reader diffs rendering instead of architecture); delta not highlighted; more than 8 components per pane; cross-pane edges
Example Scenario: chat fanout with vs without a pubsub stream: same clients and servers in both panes; only the stream and its rerouted edges differ and take the accent

Name: ML Architecture
Keywords: ml architecture; transformer; llm; moe; inference; deepseek; attention diagram
Edge Semantics: solid = tensor and token flow forward; dashed = cache reuse and routing decisions; stroke width may encode attention weight (flow-attention state)
Anti-Patterns: drawing all N layers when one representative layer plus a xN chip tells it; equal-width attention edges with weights only in labels; hiding the KV cache -- the decode story IS the cache
Example Scenario: DeepSeek-style MoE transformer decode step: tokens flow through MLA attention with KV cache reuse then top-k routed experts then the sampler

Name: Process Loop
Keywords: process; workflow; building loop; step by step; quy trình; quy trinh; iteration; how we build; how it works end to end; onboarding flow; approval flow; handoff between roles; support ticket journey
Edge Semantics: arrow = the artifact handed step to step, labelled by the artifact that MOVES (brief, PR, URL), not by the verb of the step; the closing edge to step 1 is drawn and labelled by its increment; feedback edges are dashed (async); an untaken branch stays parked at reduced opacity, its condition legible
Anti-Patterns: drawing actors as services or documents as databases (that is the system-design genre and it mislabels every box); a step drawn as a NODE instead of a beat -- a flowchart of verbs loses who does it and what moves; a loop whose closing edge teaches nothing new per cycle (decoration -- either label the increment or draw a line, not a ring); an erased untaken branch, which silently answers the question the decision asked; more than ~8 steps in one cycle
Example Scenario: a non-technical founder: the loop a team repeats to ship a feature -- brief, draft, build, deployed URL, feedback -- plus the increment on the next lap
